correctness.rationale: At strict face data the face equality projection continues to satisfy all KKT conditions in a neighborhood: the positive supported coordinates and positive complementary multipliers vary continuously. The offsets 0 and 1 already connect the bipartite support graph; changing the sign on the column-vertex rows makes B a grounded incidence matrix with full row rank. Consequently the derivative is the zero extension of the orthogonal cycle-space projector Q, and its max-entry operator norm is the maximum absolute row sum. Simultaneous translation covers each edge-displacement orbit, so there are exactly 440 rows to test. Full support independently yields the tensor square of the centering projector and hence 4(1−1/n)². A fresh exact rational replay verifies strict inequality for every proper width through n=12, the unique exception (13,7), its fraction and gap, and the sign-direction witness at step 1/1000, including the exact reported positive KKT margins. The choice of step also has a qualitative margin check: the supported displacement is at most √91 by orthogonal contraction, and a missing edge's extrapolated equality-normal change is a signed sum of at most 25 supported edge values along a bipartite path, each bounded by √91. Thus the step preserves both the positive 1/7 supported coordinates and the unit complementary slack in the starting multipliers. The positive-data ratio is a global lower bound, not an exact global norm or an unrestricted first dimension.
residual_risks: The newly run calculation verifies this finite range, not eventual behavior or arbitrary support graphs. The projector reduction is justified analytically, not inferred from the replay.
